rest.pricing.answers.invalidJson: Any endpoint that reads a body (the three creates and `POST /api/v1/pricing/vouchers/apply`), when the body is not JSON: empty, as in the example, cut short, followed by more text, or not UTF-8 (then `message` starts `the body could not be read:` instead). `Content-Type` is not checked; the body is read as JSON whatever it says. Nothing was changed; correct the body and send it again.
rest.pricing.answers.unauthorized: The three creates, when the `Authorization` header is missing, is not `Bearer` and one token, or carries a token pricing does not accept: not signed with `RS256` by a key in identity's key set, issued for another issuer or audience, more than 60 seconds past its `exp`, or not an access token (a refresh token, for instance). Pricing checks the token itself, before the `Idempotency-Key` and the body. Refresh the token pair and send the request again.
rest.pricing.answers.notFound: Any path under `/api/v1/pricing` that no endpoint serves, whatever the method: `/api/v1/pricing/health` and `/api/v1/pricing/vouchers/A/B`, for instance. Sending it again will not help.
rest.pricing.answers.methodNotAllowed: A path an endpoint serves, with a method it does not take, such as `DELETE /api/v1/pricing/discounts`. `Allow` and `message` list the methods the path takes, `HEAD` wherever `GET` is. No promotion can be changed or deleted over this API.
rest.pricing.answers.notAnObject: Any endpoint that reads a body, when the body is JSON but not an object: an array (even one holding every field in the order the field list gives), a string, a number, `true`, `false` or `null`. Fields are read by name only. Nothing was changed; send an object.
rest.pricing.answers.tooLarge: Any endpoint that reads a body, when the body is larger than 1 MiB, Rocket's JSON limit, which pricing keeps. A body with only the documented fields is far smaller.
rest.pricing.answers.internal: Any endpoint, when a database statement fails or something else happens that pricing did not expect, a crashed handler included. `traceId` is the request's `X-Request-Id`. A create is one transaction, so a create answered this way left nothing behind, and the same request with the same `Idempotency-Key` can be sent again.
rest.pricing.answers.database: Any endpoint, when pricing cannot get a connection to its database. Nothing was read or changed; retry later. A create asks the database first whether its `Idempotency-Key` was used before, so with the database down a create gets this answer even when its terms are wrong; only the token, role and `Idempotency-Key` refusals and a body that is not JSON or does not fit the endpoint are answered before it.
rest.pricing.answers.identityKeys: Any endpoint that reads a token: the three creates, and the two voucher reads when they are sent one. The token is signed with a key pricing does not hold yet, and identity's key set cannot be fetched; after a failed fetch pricing does not try again for 15 seconds. The token was not judged and nothing was changed; retry later. A voucher read sent without a token is not affected.
rest.pricing.answers.dependency: Identity or catalog fails, or does not answer within 5 seconds, when pricing has to ask it: identity for a create by a `seller` with a new `Idempotency-Key`, catalog for a create with a new key that names a product, and identity when a `seller`'s token reads a voucher that belongs to a merchant. A retry whose key already created its promotion asks neither and gets its replay. Nothing was changed; retry later.
rest.pricing.createDiscount.summary: Creates a discount: a percentage or a fixed amount off the unit price of one product, of every product in a category, or of every product, between two times. Answers the stored discount.
rest.pricing.createDiscount.who: An `admin`, whose discount is the platform's and applies to every cart; or a `seller` whose merchant identity permits to trade (status `verified` or `active`), whose discount is the merchant's and applies only to that merchant's goods. A product a seller names must be theirs in catalog. A create made with an `admin` token is written to pricing's admin audit log, refused ones included.
rest.pricing.createDiscount.field.idempo: Names this one discount: 1 to 255 characters, compared after surrounding spaces are trimmed; a fresh UUID is a good choice. Keys belong to the caller. Send the same key and the same body to retry, and a new key for every new promotion.
rest.pricing.createDiscount.field.title: The discount's name, shown to buyers. Not blank, at most 255 characters, no NUL character.
rest.pricing.createDiscount.field.value: A decimal string such as `"15"`, or a JSON number: greater than zero, at most two decimal places, below 10,000,000,000. For `PERCENTAGE` it is the percent off, at most 100; for `FIXED` it is the rupiah taken off each unit. A unit is never priced below zero.
rest.pricing.createDiscount.field.target: The SKU of the one product the discount applies to. Not blank, at most 100 characters, no NUL character. Catalog must know the product, and a seller's must be theirs. Leave out both targets, or send `null`, for a discount on every product.

The slug of a catalog category, such as `footwear`: the discount applies to every product in it. Same length rules as `target_product_id`; it is not checked against catalog. With both targets set, a product matching either one gets the discount.
rest.pricing.createDiscount.field.startT: When the discount starts: an RFC 3339 date-time with an offset, such as `2026-11-01T00:00:00Z`. It may be in the past, and must be before `end_time`.
rest.pricing.createDiscount.field.endTim: When the discount ends: an RFC 3339 date-time with an offset, in the future and after `start_time`. The discount is in force from `start_time` to `end_time`, both included.
rest.pricing.createDiscount.case.created: The discount is stored and in force between its two times. `merchant_principal_id` is the seller's merchant, or `null` for an admin's discount. Amounts come back as strings with two decimal places. Keep `id`: no endpoint changes or ends a discount early.
rest.pricing.createDiscount.case.replaye: This caller sent the same `Idempotency-Key` with the same body before, and that request created a discount. `Idempotent-Replayed: true` marks the answer; the body is that discount, and nothing new was created. The key is looked up before anything else is checked, so the replay comes back even after `end_time` has passed, the seller's merchant has stopped trading, catalog has dropped the product, or while identity or catalog is down. Bodies are compared after parsing, so key order and spacing do not matter, but `15` and `"15.00"` are different values.
rest.pricing.createDiscount.case.keyMiss: The `Idempotency-Key` header is missing, empty or only spaces. Nothing was created; send the request again with a key.
rest.pricing.createDiscount.case.keyTooL: The `Idempotency-Key` header is longer than 255 characters. Nothing was created; send a shorter key.
rest.pricing.createDiscount.case.terms: The body parses, but a value breaks a rule in the field descriptions; here `start_time` is after `end_time`. `message` names the first rule that failed. Nothing was created and the key is still free: correct the body and send it again with the same key.
rest.pricing.createDiscount.case.role: The token is valid, but its role is neither `admin` nor `seller`.
rest.pricing.createDiscount.case.noMerch: The caller is a `seller`, and identity has no merchant for the account.
rest.pricing.createDiscount.case.notTrad: The seller's merchant is not permitted to trade: identity permits it only while the merchant's status is `verified` or `active`, so a new merchant waits for an admin's approval.
rest.pricing.createDiscount.case.notYour: A `seller` named, in `target_product_id`, a product catalog lists under another merchant.
rest.pricing.createDiscount.case.noProdu: Catalog does not know the product in `target_product_id`. Checked for an `admin` too.
rest.pricing.createDiscount.case.invalid: The body is JSON but does not fit the endpoint: a field is missing or has the wrong JSON type, `discount_type` is not one of its two values, or a time is not an RFC 3339 date-time. `message` starts with the field's name, then the reason and the position in the body; here `discount_type` was sent as `PERCENT`. A missing field is reported for the whole body instead, starting `the body does not match this endpoint:`.
rest.pricing.createDiscount.case.keyReus: This caller has already used the `Idempotency-Key` for a different body, or for another kind of promotion. The key is looked up before the body's terms are checked and before identity or catalog is asked, so this answer comes first. Nothing was created. Send a new key to create a new discount; to retry the earlier request, resend its body unchanged.
rest.pricing.listDiscounts.summary: Lists every discount in force now, platform and merchant discounts alike, newest first, in one array without paging.
rest.pricing.listDiscounts.case.listed: Every discount that is active and whose window contains the time of the request, ordered by `created_at`, newest first; an empty array when there is none. A discount with a `merchant_principal_id` applies only to that merchant's goods, one with `null` to every cart. When several match a unit, checkout applies the one that saves the most, and none to a unit it prices at a flash sale.
rest.pricing.createVoucher.summary: Creates a voucher: a code a buyer enters at checkout for a percentage or a fixed amount off the goods, with a minimum spend, an optional cap, a quota of orders and an expiry. A voucher never reduces the shipping fee. Answers the stored voucher.
rest.pricing.createVoucher.who: An `admin`, whose voucher is the platform's and applies to every cart; or a `seller` whose merchant identity permits to trade (status `verified` or `active`), whose voucher applies only to that merchant's carts. A create made with an `admin` token is written to pricing's admin audit log, refused ones included.
rest.pricing.createVoucher.field.idempot: Names this one voucher: 1 to 255 characters, compared after surrounding spaces are trimmed; a fresh UUID is a good choice. Keys belong to the caller. Send the same key and the same body to retry, and a new key for every new promotion.
rest.pricing.createVoucher.field.code: The code buyers type. It is stored in upper case and matched without regard to case everywhere, so `harbolnas25` and `HARBOLNAS25` are one code. After upper-casing: not blank, at most 100 characters, no NUL character, no whitespace at either end. Unique across every merchant's vouchers, expired and used-up ones included.
rest.pricing.createVoucher.field.title: The voucher's name, shown to buyers. Not blank, at most 255 characters, no NUL character.
rest.pricing.createVoucher.field.value: A decimal string or a JSON number: greater than zero, at most two decimal places, below 10,000,000,000. For `PERCENTAGE` it is the percent off the cart's goods, at most 100; for `FIXED` it is the rupiah taken off. The discount never exceeds the goods subtotal.
rest.pricing.createVoucher.field.minSpen: The goods subtotal, in rupiah, a cart must reach for the voucher to apply: zero or more, at most two decimal places, below 10,000,000,000. Required; send `"0"` for no minimum.
rest.pricing.createVoucher.field.maxDisc: The most the voucher takes off, in rupiah: greater than zero, at most two decimal places, below 10,000,000,000. `null`, or left out, for no cap.
rest.pricing.createVoucher.field.quota: How many orders may use the voucher: an integer from 1 to 2,147,483,647. Each order placed with the voucher counts once.
rest.pricing.createVoucher.field.expires: When the voucher stops applying: an RFC 3339 date-time with an offset, in the future.
rest.pricing.createVoucher.case.created: The voucher is stored and usable, with `code` in upper case and `used_count` 0. `merchant_principal_id` is the seller's merchant, or `null` for an admin's voucher. Amounts come back as strings with two decimal places.
rest.pricing.createVoucher.case.replayed: This caller sent the same `Idempotency-Key` with the same body before, and that request created a voucher. `Idempotent-Replayed: true` marks the answer; the body is that voucher as it is now, `used_count` included, and nothing new was created. The key is looked up before anything else is checked, so the replay comes back even after `expires_at` has passed, the seller's merchant has stopped trading, or while identity is down. Bodies are compared after parsing and after the code is upper-cased, so key order, spacing and the code's case do not matter, but `25000` and `"25000.00"` are different values.
rest.pricing.createVoucher.case.keyMissi: The `Idempotency-Key` header is missing, empty or only spaces. Nothing was created; send the request again with a key.
rest.pricing.createVoucher.case.keyTooLo: The `Idempotency-Key` header is longer than 255 characters. Nothing was created; send a shorter key.
rest.pricing.createVoucher.case.terms: The body parses, but a value breaks a rule in the field descriptions; here `max_discount` is `"0"`. `message` names the first rule that failed. Nothing was created and the key is still free: correct the body and send it again with the same key.
rest.pricing.createVoucher.case.role: The token is valid, but its role is neither `admin` nor `seller`.
rest.pricing.createVoucher.case.noMercha: The caller is a `seller`, and identity has no merchant for the account.
rest.pricing.createVoucher.case.notTradi: The seller's merchant is not permitted to trade: identity permits it only while the merchant's status is `verified` or `active`, so a new merchant waits for an admin's approval.
rest.pricing.createVoucher.case.codeTake: A voucher with this code exists already, compared without regard to case, whoever owns it and whether or not it has expired or run out. Nothing was created and the key is still free: choose another code and send the request again with the same key.
rest.pricing.createVoucher.case.invalidB: The body is JSON but does not fit the endpoint: a field is missing or has the wrong JSON type, `discount_type` is not one of its two values, `quota` is not a 32-bit integer, or `expires_at` is not an RFC 3339 date-time. `message` starts with the field's name, then the reason and the position in the body; here `quota` was sent as the string `"500"`. A missing field is reported for the whole body instead, starting `the body does not match this endpoint:`.
rest.pricing.createVoucher.case.keyReuse: This caller has already used the `Idempotency-Key` for a different body, or for another kind of promotion. The key is looked up before the body's terms are checked and before identity or catalog is asked, so this answer comes first. Nothing was created. Send a new key to create a new voucher; to retry the earlier request, resend its body unchanged.
rest.pricing.applyVoucher.summary: Checks a voucher code against a cart before checkout, as checkout would: answers the voucher's terms when it would apply, and `null` when it would not. Reserves nothing and takes no quota.
rest.pricing.applyVoucher.who: Anyone; the token is optional. An `admin`, or a `seller` whose merchant owns the voucher, also sees its quota and use. No token, or one that does not verify, reads as a buyer. A call made with an `admin` token is written to pricing's admin audit log.
rest.pricing.applyVoucher.field.code: The code as the buyer typed it, not blank. Matched without regard to case, but otherwise exactly: surrounding spaces make it unknown.
rest.pricing.applyVoucher.field.cartSubt: The cart's goods subtotal in rupiah, before the voucher: a decimal string or a JSON number. The voucher applies only when it is greater than zero and at least the voucher's `min_spend`. Checkout compares `min_spend` with the subtotal after flash sales and discounts, so send that figure to get the answer checkout will give.
rest.pricing.applyVoucher.field.merchant: The merchant whose goods are in the cart: the `merchant_principal_id` catalog gives on each product. A merchant's voucher applies only when this names that merchant; a platform voucher applies whatever it is. Left out or `null`, only platform vouchers apply.
rest.pricing.applyVoucher.case.buyerView: The voucher is active, unexpired, has quota left and fits this cart, and the caller is a buyer or sent no token. Quota and use are left out. It is not a promise: the last of the quota can go to another order before this one is placed.
rest.pricing.applyVoucher.case.ownerView: As above, and the token is an `admin`'s, or a `seller`'s whose merchant owns the voucher: the whole voucher, `quota` and `used_count` included.
rest.pricing.applyVoucher.case.none: No voucher would apply: the code is unknown, switched off, expired or used up, the subtotal is zero or below `min_spend`, or the voucher belongs to a merchant other than `merchant_principal_id`. The body is `null`, and it does not say which.
rest.pricing.applyVoucher.case.invalidBo: The body is JSON but does not fit the endpoint: a field is missing or has the wrong JSON type, or an amount is not a number. `message` starts with the field's name, then the reason and the position in the body; here `cart_subtotal` was sent as `"Rp150.000"`. A missing field is reported for the whole body instead, starting `the body does not match this endpoint:`.
rest.pricing.getVoucher.summary: Reads a voucher by its code. Only a voucher that can still be used is found.
rest.pricing.getVoucher.who: Anyone; the token is optional. An `admin`, or a `seller` whose merchant owns the voucher, also sees its quota and use. No token, or one that does not verify, reads as a buyer. A call made with an `admin` token is written to pricing's admin audit log.
rest.pricing.getVoucher.field.code: The voucher's code, matched without regard to case. Percent-encode any character a path segment cannot carry.
rest.pricing.getVoucher.case.buyerView: The voucher is active, unexpired and has quota left, and the caller is a buyer or sent no token: its terms without quota and use. Whether it fits a cart is not checked here; `POST /api/v1/pricing/vouchers/apply` does that.
rest.pricing.getVoucher.case.ownerView: As above, and the token is an `admin`'s, or a `seller`'s whose merchant owns the voucher: the whole voucher, `quota` and `used_count` included.
rest.pricing.getVoucher.case.notFound: No usable voucher has this code: there is none, or it is switched off, expired or used up. `message` repeats the code as it was sent.
rest.pricing.createFlashSale.summary: Creates a flash sale: a fixed unit price for one product between two times, for a limited number of units. Answers the stored sale.
rest.pricing.createFlashSale.who: An `admin`, for any product catalog knows; or a `seller` whose merchant identity permits to trade (status `verified` or `active`), for a product that is theirs in catalog. A create made with an `admin` token is written to pricing's admin audit log, refused ones included.
rest.pricing.createFlashSale.field.idemp: Names this one flash sale: 1 to 255 characters, compared after surrounding spaces are trimmed; a fresh UUID is a good choice. Keys belong to the caller. Send the same key and the same body to retry, and a new key for every new promotion.
rest.pricing.createFlashSale.field.title: The sale's name, shown to buyers. Not blank, at most 255 characters, no NUL character.
rest.pricing.createFlashSale.field.produ: The SKU of the product on sale. Not blank, at most 100 characters, no NUL character. Catalog must know it, and a seller's must be theirs.
rest.pricing.createFlashSale.field.flash: The unit price during the sale, in rupiah: a decimal string or a JSON number, greater than zero, at most two decimal places, below 10,000,000,000. A cart pays it only when it is below the product's own price.
rest.pricing.createFlashSale.field.stock: How many units may sell at the flash price: an integer from 1 to 2,147,483,647.
rest.pricing.createFlashSale.field.start: When the sale opens: an RFC 3339 date-time with an offset, such as `2026-11-11T02:00:00Z`. It may be in the past, and must be before `end_time`.
rest.pricing.createFlashSale.field.endTi: When the sale closes: an RFC 3339 date-time with an offset, in the future and after `start_time`.
rest.pricing.createFlashSale.case.create: The sale is stored and active, with `stock_sold` 0. `merchant_principal_id` is the seller's merchant, or `null` for an admin's sale. `flash_price` comes back as a string with two decimal places.
rest.pricing.createFlashSale.case.replay: This caller sent the same `Idempotency-Key` with the same body before, and that request created a flash sale. `Idempotent-Replayed: true` marks the answer; the body is that sale as it is now, `stock_sold` included, and nothing new was created. The key is looked up before anything else is checked, so the replay comes back even after `end_time` has passed, the seller's merchant has stopped trading, catalog has dropped the product, or while identity or catalog is down. Bodies are compared after parsing, so key order and spacing do not matter, but `349000` and `"349000.00"` are different values.
rest.pricing.createFlashSale.case.keyMis: The `Idempotency-Key` header is missing, empty or only spaces. Nothing was created; send the request again with a key.
rest.pricing.createFlashSale.case.keyToo: The `Idempotency-Key` header is longer than 255 characters. Nothing was created; send a shorter key.
rest.pricing.createFlashSale.case.terms: The body parses, but a value breaks a rule in the field descriptions; here `stock_limit` is 0. `message` names the first rule that failed. Nothing was created and the key is still free: correct the body and send it again with the same key.
rest.pricing.createFlashSale.case.role: The token is valid, but its role is neither `admin` nor `seller`.
rest.pricing.createFlashSale.case.noMerc: The caller is a `seller`, and identity has no merchant for the account.
rest.pricing.createFlashSale.case.notTra: The seller's merchant is not permitted to trade: identity permits it only while the merchant's status is `verified` or `active`, so a new merchant waits for an admin's approval.
rest.pricing.createFlashSale.case.notYou: A `seller` named, in `product_id`, a product catalog lists under another merchant.
rest.pricing.createFlashSale.case.noProd: Catalog does not know the product in `product_id`. Checked for an `admin` too.
rest.pricing.createFlashSale.case.invali: The body is JSON but does not fit the endpoint: a field is missing or has the wrong JSON type, `stock_limit` is not a 32-bit integer, or a time is not an RFC 3339 date-time. Here `stock_limit` was left out, and a missing field is reported for the whole body; a field with a wrong value starts `message` with its own name instead, then the reason and the position in the body.
rest.pricing.createFlashSale.case.keyReu: This caller has already used the `Idempotency-Key` for a different body, or for another kind of promotion. The key is looked up before the body's terms are checked and before identity or catalog is asked, so this answer comes first. Nothing was created. Send a new key to create a new flash sale; to retry the earlier request, resend its body unchanged.
rest.pricing.getFlashSale.summary: Reads the flash sale a buyer of one product gets now.
rest.pricing.getFlashSale.field.productI: The product's SKU, exactly as catalog has it; case matters.
rest.pricing.getFlashSale.case.onSale: A sale of this product is active, open now, and has at least one unit left. With several, the lowest `flash_price` wins, then the oldest sale. `stock_limit` minus `stock_sold` is the number of units left at that price.
rest.pricing.getFlashSale.case.none: No sale of this product is open now with a unit left. The body is `null`, not an error.
